caption:
Stop buying things "for the tax deduction". Do this maths first.

A deduction is not a refund. It lowers your taxable income, so what you get back is your tax rate on the amount. On the 30% rate ($45,001 to $135,000 in 2026–27) that's 30c per dollar, plus the 2% Medicare levy.

So a $1,000 laptop for work:
- You spend $1,000.
- Your tax drops by about $320.
- You're still $680 out of pocket.

And a work item that costs more than $300 is generally claimed over its effective life, not all in one year.

When is it worth it? When you needed the thing for work anyway. Then the deduction is a discount on something you were buying. It's never free.

Who told you "just claim it on tax"?

Narrated by an AI voice.

#taxdeductions #taxreturn #australiantax #paylesslegally #moneytips
figures_checked: Resident rates 2026–27: nil to $18,200; 15c to $45,000; $4,020 + 30c to $135,000; $31,020 + 37c to $190,000; $51,370 + 45c above; Medicare levy 2% not included (ATO Tax rates – Australian residents, checked 15 Nov 2026)

Work items costing $300 or less can be claimed immediately; over $300 claimed as decline in value over the effective life (ATO Fixed rate method page, 'what you can claim separately', checked 15 Nov 2026)
